eligibility.quote: I notice in the logs "terminate called without an active exception" - which usually means that a std::thread went out of scope while not joined/stopped - I notice we have a std::thread in this test - but I don't actually see how it could go out of scope...
eligibility.reason: E1 is satisfied by a concrete CI failure with a maintainer's verbatim error-log observation; neither a deterministic reproducer nor a known root cause is required. The specification's E1 failure is therefore unsupported. The case still cannot pass E2 step 1: the retained evidence does not identify which interaction, assertion or pair caused the abort. The speculative std::thread explanation is not sufficient to affirm an internal root cause at step 2. E3 remains unestablished; E4 documents the CI failure but not a particular failed interface.

loudness.reason: Retain the excluded-case null. The abort diagnostic is documented; it does not identify an early interface rejection.

detection_stage.reason: The failure appears in test execution, but an eligible composition has not been established, so the null field remains appropriate.

resolution.quote: I haven't seen this one lately. Are we still running into this? Maybe it really was an unrelated threading issue somewhere...
resolution.reason: Retain null after exclusion. Closing an intermittent issue after non-recurrence is not an observed repair of its composition.

notes: Disagree with the reasons/gate, not with retaining this case outside the eligible set. The test source at 58f3828224f051b40ce0b66d217ae4335703a5d2 explicitly exercises topic-based RDF loading and creates spinning_thread before assertions and join; this allows several explanations and does not prove which assertion or interaction failed. I read PRs #1348, #1411, #1422 and #1458: their comments identify #1334 as an unrelated CI failure, not a fix. PR #1384 and its diff detach a thread in planning_scene_rviz_plugin, a different path; they do not show this RDF-loader test repaired. No missing failure class can be responsibly invented.
